newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE appoints coordinator for Albania aid efforts.
newsitem.headline: OSCE appoints coordinator for Albania aid efforts.

text.p: Europe's top security body said on Friday it had appointed an Austrian diplomat to coordinate a three-pronged international relief effort on the ground in chaos-torn Albania.
European mediator Franz Vranitzky told a news briefing that Herbert Grubmayr had been chosen as the Organisation for Security and Cooperation (OSCE) administrator in the troubled Balkan state.

"Grubmayr will be a coordinating and contact point for three pillars -- the OSCE, the European Union and a multinational protection force," the former Austrian chancellor said after a meeting with the OSCE permanent council.
Vranitzky highlighted six key aims of the international community, as approved by the Vienna-based council:
- to support the present government in Albania under the National Council of Reconciliation.
- to restore public security through a multinational protection force.
- to further dialogue and cooperation between individual political groupings in Albania on the condition that all involved supported the principles of democracy.
- to provide humanitarian and economic aid through EU channels
- to prepare for and monitor fresh elections in June
- to support the restoration of press freedom and freedom of speech.

Vranitzky said that the goals could not be fulfilled individually. "All of these activities are dependent on one another. The holding of these elections will not be possible in chaos and anarchy," he said.
"The most important task is to protect humanitarian and economic aid and ensure that it does not get into the hands of illegitimate groups," he added.
Italian advance units of the multinational military force arrived on Friday in Albania, where violence erupted following the collapse of a number of shady pyramid investment schemes.
Vranitzky said he and Grubmayr would travel to Albania next Wednesday to prepare the ground for an OSCE mission. He would probably stay there two days, he added.
Vranitzky stressed that the OSCE would consider the present government of Prime Minister Bashkim Fino as its sole negotiating partner.
"If the Fino government thinks it is useful to deal with the citizen's committees then they will do it. We cannot interfere in that," he said.

Vranitzky said the force had no mandate to disarm locals in the first phase of the relief effort, but he hoped they would be encouraged to surrender their weapons when they saw that the situation was safer.
